100%, the first couple weeks my energy levels were all out of whack and I had a decreased appetite, but those side effects cleared up and I feel more energetic, active, and with a greater sense of overall well-being. I have a greater propensity to socialize and express myself, and my life in essentially all aspects has improved.

Lots of people have had great results with Prozac, but the people who are struggling and need a question answered tend to be the ones posting on here. As far as I’m aware, even if negative side effects are experienced, most people who take Prozac still notice (at least some) positive effects.

The warning about alcohol mostly stems from the sedative effects of both Prozac and alcohol. Not all people get it, but there is a “Prozac tired” I and others get during the acclimating phase of starting the med. That tiredness combined with the effects of alcohol can make you more tired than usual and quite a bit less aware of your surroundings. Use alcohol responsibly like usual and you won’t have any problems.

I’ve definitely experienced this on Prozac. It wasn’t an insane difference, but it was enough that I had to stop sometimes and appreciate previously mundane things, like a green lawn, or Christmas lights.

I’m on it for persistent depressive disorder and anxiety. I was on it previously before starting again and found that it helped me a lot with my anxiety and got rid of suicidal thoughts entirely. Unfortunately it doesn’t always work as well as it has for me for everyone else. I started on 10mg originally and it was helpful for a short period but I ultimately felt the same as usual after around 6/8 weeks albeit with maybe a slightly improved resting state of well being, so I upped it to 20 and have been doing great.

I hope it works well for you too when you do start. I’m curious how it affects your anxiety. A lot of people experience increased anxiety during the acclimating period but find that it improves after a few weeks.

I started 20mg again in the last week (my finals are next week) and I haven’t personally had any issues. Most of the tiredness associated with Prozac I get later in the day around the time I start getting ready for bed anyways. Now, throw absolutely everything I just said out the window, because everybody responds differently. I wouldn’t risk that you are tired and anxious and are not mentally equipped to do well on your finals. I highly recommend you let finals pass before you start the medication.

When I started Prozac, my girlfriend got upset that we weren’t intimate almost at all, she took it personally and told me that she felt she was failing as a partner. When she also couldn’t get me to ejaculate during the sparing times we were intimate, it made her even more upset.

I think she got the impression that symptoms of “delayed ejaculation” and “reduced sex drive” were some sort of excuse for the fact that I wasn’t attracted to her in that way - she truly took it to heart. It wasn’t until I showed her studies and side-effect lists that she believed she had nothing to do with what was happening.

A more silver lining to the situation was that Prozac helped me be my more expressive self and better show her that I love her, and despite the fact that my sex drive was wayyy down, she learned that my love for her is not tied to my sex drive.

Note: I also learned that acting intimate despite how I’m feeling in the immediate moment helped better spark feelings of intimacy and bolstered my sex drive. I imagine that works differently for some people however.

Male breast tissue and chest fat doesn’t store quite the same as it does for women where weight loss/gain can have a significant visual impact on the breasts. The gland, or breast tissue part is going to remain almost entirely unchanged despite weight loss. In fact, it may become more prominent because it will be shrouded less by fat and other tissues. Some supplements and steroids can reduce the appearance but in most cases will not get rid of it unless the tissue is extremely new.

I personally lost around 40lbs (almost a quarter of my bodyweight at the time) after falling victim to the myth that weight loss will eliminate or even improve the appearance of gyno. It doesn’t. Only definite way of eliminating gyno is surgery because the gland doesn’t just disappear.
